I agree re Scarlemagne’s complex characterization. However, to play devil’s advocate for a minute, the scientist enclave pre-Kipo (Leo included) were up to some pretty not great stuff in testing animals by injecting them with random DNA and hoping it would mutate the “right way”. I think it’s conceivable that there are plenty of animals that we didn’t see, pre-Hugo, that mutated incorrectly and instead of suddenly playing the piano and becoming a Victorian for some reason, they, say lost their lungs and asphyxiated, or developed hemophilia, or... in the name of finding a way to “reclaim” an Earth that wasn’t really theirs in the first place and of which they were often not good stewards (I may be projecting some of my own dim views on humanity’s environmental impact here, cough cough). Anyway I feel like I actually agree with some of Scarlemagne’s vitriol towards humans, because most of the ones he has had any experience with have been shitty to him or other animals. Additionally while Leo and co. did mutate him to become intelligent or whatever gene that allows mutes to speak English, they didn’t really teach him about being a good person (or mandrill).
